stages.title: Ingest
stages.what: Before the model sees a complaint, we check it is usable. It must not be empty, must not be over 2,000 characters, and must contain letters. A bad message is refused with a clear reason and nothing is stored.
stages.why: Refusing bad input at the door keeps every later step simple. The answer tells the sender exactly what to fix. Nothing about a refused message is kept.

stages.title: Clean
stages.what: Emails, phone numbers, card numbers and account numbers become placeholders such as [CARD]. A 16-digit number counts as a card only if it passes the Luhn check, the checksum banks use, so an order number is not hidden by mistake. Then the text is lower-cased and spaces are tidied, and only this cleaned text is stored.
stages.why: Personal data never reaches the model or the database. Regular patterns can be read and tested line by line, which a learned detector cannot offer. The same function cleans the training text and the live text, so the model sees the same kind of text in both places.
stages.code:
def clean(text: str) -> CleanResult:
    """Mask personal data, then normalise: NFKC, one space between words, lower-case.

    NFKC runs first so look-alike digits (full-width) cannot slip past the masks.
    Devanagari is kept as is. Running clean twice gives the same text.
    """
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
    masked, pii = redact(text)
    masked = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", masked).strip()
    masked = _lower_keep_placeholders(masked)
    return CleanResult(masked, pii, len(masked), len(_WORD.findall(masked)))

stages.title: Classify
stages.what: TF-IDF gives each word and short group of letters a score: high if it is frequent in this message and rare overall. Logistic regression holds one weight per term per intent, adds up score times weight, and softmax turns the 77 totals into probabilities that sum to one. The scores are divided by one number fitted on validation data (temperature 0.59) so a 90% answer is right about 90% of the time.
stages.why: On the held-out test set this model scores macro-F1 0.900; the small neural network in the Compare tab scores 0.887. The linear model is slightly better and fully explainable, so it serves. Both are reported.

stages.title: Explain
stages.what: For a linear model the explanation is exact. The score of an intent is a sum of weight times TF-IDF value, one term per word, so we show the five largest terms. Terms starting with ~ are groups of letters; they are hidden when they only repeat a word already shown.
stages.why: A reviewer can see why the model answered, not only what it answered. If the terms look wrong the reviewer can tell at a glance. The terms plus a fixed offset add up to the real score, so nothing is hidden.
stages.code:
def explain(self, text: str, intent: str, k: int = 5) -> list[dict]:
    """The k terms that pushed hardest towards `intent`: weight = coefficient x TF-IDF value.

    Character pieces are shown with a leading "~". Weights plus the intercept add up
    to the intent's raw score before softmax, so nothing is hidden.
    """
    row = self._features([text])
    coef = self.coef[INTENTS.index(intent)]
    pairs = [(float(coef[j] * v), j) for j, v in zip(row.indices, row.data)]
    best = heapq.nlargest(k, pairs)
    return [{"term": self._names[j], "weight": w} for w, j in best]

stages.title: Route
stages.what: A table maps each of the 77 intents to one of 7 teams and to an urgency. The probability of a team is the sum of the probabilities of its intents. If the best team has less than 0.70 probability, or many words are unknown and the team is not clear (above 0.20 unknown, team under 0.97), a person looks. A ticket is urgent when the chance of the high-urgency intents reaches 0.20.
stages.why: Two cards intents can be confusing and still be one team, so summing is safer than trusting one intent. The urgent cut-off was chosen on validation data to catch at least 97% of urgent tickets (98.3% on test), accepting some false alarms, because missing a fraud report costs more than a wasted look. Team and urgency come from this project's own table, not from the dataset.

stages.title: Review
stages.what: Tickets the model is unsure about wait in a queue, urgent first, then oldest. A person confirms the answer or picks the right intent, and the decision is saved with who, when and a note. A unique rule in the database and a transaction make sure two people cannot both decide the same ticket; the second gets a clear 'already reviewed' reply.
stages.why: These rows are the override log and the training data for the next model. Only uncertain tickets are reviewed, so they are a biased sample and say little about the whole stream. Nothing here trains or promotes a model; a person runs that step and a frozen test decides.

stages.title: Monitor
stages.what: A model is trained on yesterday's messages. We compare the latest 500 live tickets with the validation tickets on things we can measure now: message length, share of unknown words, the model's confidence and the mix of teams. PSI sums (live share - reference share) x ln(live share / reference share) over bins; under 0.1 is stable and over 0.25 is a real shift.
stages.why: True labels arrive late, so these signals warn early. Drift is a reason to look, not proof the model is wrong. With fewer than 200 live tickets the page says there is not enough data instead of guessing.
stages.code:
def psi(expected: np.ndarray, actual: np.ndarray, bins=10) -> float:
    """Population Stability Index of two samples.

    `bins` is a number of reference-quantile bins or an array of edges. Both samples use
    the same edges, taken from the reference, so the bins mean the same thing for both.
    """
    expected, actual = np.asarray(expected, float), np.asarray(actual, float)
    edges = bin_edges(expected, bins) if np.isscalar(bins) else np.asarray(bins, float)
    return psi_from_shares(_shares(expected, edges), _shares(actual, edges))

limits: Team and urgency come from this project's rubric, not from the dataset.
Banking77 labels contain noise; about 8% of sampled train labels were disputed in the data audit.
English only: Hinglish and Devanagari text is mostly sent to a human or misrouted.
